messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things are holding, but just barely—like a roof with too many leaks, patched up but still creaking. The regime’s still in charge, but the cracks are showing in the way they’re scrambling to keep things together. Let’s stay sharp, but not reckless—this isn’t the time to push, but it might be the time to get ready."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to peel—small cracks, nothing that’ll bring the house down yet. The guards are still at their posts, but someone’s been whispering in the back rooms, and the fuel’s getting expensive for no good reason. Keep your eyes open, but don’t reach for the hammer just yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the cracks are showing in weird little ways—like when the boss suddenly ghosts you or the graffiti stays up too long. The money’s there for now, but the whispers are getting louder, and the security guys seem jumpy. Not a storm yet, but the wind’s shifting."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—quietly, where only a few of us notice. The air feels heavier in the capital, but out in the provinces, life goes on like nothing’s changed. For now, the machine hums, but the gears are grinding a little louder than they used to."*"
Sender 5: "*"The ship’s drifting, not sinking—yet. Checkpoints are thinning, but the real cracks are in the backrooms: no one’s at the wheel, the money’s drying up, and the streets are testing limits without pushback. Keep your ears open—this isn’t chaos, it’s a slow unraveling. And if the markets are betting on stability? They’re either blind or already have an exit plan."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are shaking—but not all at once. The usual players are stuck in their own corners, the streets are quieter than they seem, and even the doctors are passing notes. Something’s coming, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’ll know when the time is right."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are cracking, but the paint’s still wet—no one’s sure if it’s just the heat or the foundation. The old hands are being pushed aside, the soldiers are laughing too loud, and the watch groups are talking politics instead of theft. But the buses keep running, the money’s still flowing, and the diplomats are packing their bags *just in case*. My gut says the regime’s holding its breath, not its cards—let’s stay sharp, but not so sharp it cuts us."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the guards are the ones looking away. We’re not there yet, but the question isn’t *if* the wind changes, just *when* and how hard it hits."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—like we’re all holding our breath, waiting for something to break. The regime’s still standing, but it’s not the same quiet control as before; it’s more like a house of cards trying not to wobble. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything—this could go either way, and we might not see it coming until it’s already here."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels charged, but no one’s sure which way it’ll break—some are whispering about cracks, others say the walls are still holding. The real question isn’t if things will move, but what’ll push them over the edge first."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like the walls are holding for now—no cracks, just the usual quiet hum of things being swept under the rug. But the air feels heavier than usual, like everyone’s holding their breath waiting for the next move. Stay sharp, and let’s keep this circle tight."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like the calm before something, but no one’s sure what. The usual channels are holding, but the cost is showing, and the business crowd is playing it careful. Not panic, just… hedging. Keep your ears open, but don’t let the surface fool you—there’s a current running underneath."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things feel like they’re holding for now, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—security’s getting nervous, the money’s still flowing, and the streets are quiet but not quiet enough. The real question is whether they’re just too busy patting themselves on the back to notice the rot underneath."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a rope fraying one strand at a time. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in the little things: slower decisions, patrols pulling back from trouble spots, even the censors scrambling to keep up. No one’s running for the exits yet, but everyone’s bracing for the next gust of wind. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, and the wrong push could unravel it all."*"
Sender 15: "*"Something’s shifting—small cracks, but they’re spreading. The reshuffle reversal, the leave being allowed, the silence at the meeting—it’s not just frustration anymore, it’s like everyone’s holding their breath. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet. We’ll talk soon."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are shaking—you can feel it in the way the guards eye each other now, in the way the shelves stay full but the fuel pumps cough. The old men in the back rooms are still talking, but not to each other anymore. Something’s coming, but whether it’s a storm or just the calm before the next crackdown… well, we’ll know soon enough. Stay sharp, and keep your ears open—this isn’t over, but it’s not the same either."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—people are whispering more, but only when they’re sure the door is closed. The regime’s still in control, but the gears are grinding slower, and the ones who should know are starting to ask quiet questions. Let’s keep our eyes open and our mouths careful."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The old guard is still in charge, but the water’s rising, and no one’s sure how long the patches will last. Keep your ears open, your plans quiet, and your bags packed—just in case."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but the air’s different—like everyone’s waiting for the other shoe to drop. The regime’s still got its tricks, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. We’ll know more when the next move comes."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things feel like they’re balanced on a knife’s edge—no one’s backing down, but no one’s rushing to strike first either. The air’s different now: people are talking, but quietly, like they’re testing how far they can lean before something gives. Stay sharp, but don’t let fear make the decision for you."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—no panic in the ranks, but the old hands are being pushed aside, and the money’s still flowing like nothing’s wrong. The streets are buzzing with talk, but the embassies aren’t packing up yet. My gut says they’ve got time, but the cracks are there—just not the kind that break all at once."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels thick—like the quiet before a storm, but no one’s sure if it’s rain or just the wind shifting. The old hands are telling us to stay still, but the kids are getting itchy, and the regime’s moving pieces like they’re expecting something. Let’s keep our ears open, but no sudden moves—we don’t want to be the ones who misread the room."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are there—just harder to see. The regime’s playing it cool, but the quiet ones are starting to move, and that’s when things get dangerous. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are holding for now—no cracks, just the usual quiet hum of things being swept under the rug. People are hedging their bets, but the regime’s still got its rhythm, even if the teachers’ paychecks are running late. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to bet on anything."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The usual cracks are there, but they’re patching them faster than we’d expect. Still, the taxi drivers are whispering what we’ve all been thinking, and that’s never a good sign for them. Keep your ears open, but don’t let your hands get too steady—this isn’t over, just quieter than it should be."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
